title: Crosswalk: the second grid against the first (2026-10-06)

links.why: The box was a branch first, and the template ships the box, never a tree.
Both are about what leaves the box once it's open.
A template is a box that's complete when you open it.
The nine dots say go past the edge. The rule says look inside first, and only then go outside.
More contents than boxes means two share one. That's why h16 hashes were too short and became h256.
The model sees inside its own scope only; code checks a citation's form, and a witness checks it's true.
An unopened box isn't empty and isn't full. It's not_asked, which is why the states are never collapsed.
Everyone holds only their own box, so what passes between boxes is pointers, not contents.
Boxes inside boxes until the cows come home: the grids themselves. A full grid starts a new one instead of growing forever.
It worked because everyone agreed the size. The socket standard is the same bet.
Kart and bubblewrap are the sandbox.
Picture and compare.
Sequencing: what goes in first carries the rest.
